html:
A Samoyedic people of the Russian Arctic, the largest of the Siberian tundra peoples, shown on the map in 1530 on the Yamal and Gydan peninsulas east of the Urals. They also lived west of the Urals along the coast toward the White Sea.

The Nenets are known for reindeer herding on a large scale, with families travelling hundreds of kilometres a year between winter forest and summer tundra and living in skin tents. Russians long called them Samoyeds.

Traders from Novgorod were reaching the far north for furs well before 1500, and after Moscow absorbed Novgorod it took over the trade. During the Russian conquest of Siberia the Nenets paid fur tribute and sometimes rose against it. Their neighbours were the Khanty and Komi to the south and the Enets and Nganasan to the east. Herding still goes on today on the Yamal Peninsula, beside huge gas fields.
